To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the efficiency of human immunodeficiency (HIV) virus infection of cells lacking the protein PDZD8 is comparable to that of PDZD8-expressed cells.
PDZD8 can be eliminated from cells by CRISPR-Cas9, and that PDZD8-knocked-out cells are infected by retroviruses with the same efficiency as the parental PDZDs8-expressing cell line.
PDZD8 can be knocked out in human cells and that the efficiency of HIV-1 and MLV infection is not decreased in the resulting PDZD8-knocked out cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the study of HIV-1 infection.
the role of the PDZD8 gene in retrovirus infection.
understanding the molecular basis of retroviral infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PDZD8 does not appear to be an essential factor for HIV-1 and MLV infection.
PDZD8 plays a minor role in the HIV-1 life cycle and that its role is not critical to the virus.
PDZD8 has been shown to be a host factor that can bind HIV capsid protein, and that its expression level can influence HIV infectivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PDZD8 can be considered a non-essential factor in the retroviral life cycle, at least for HIV-1 and MLV.
PDZD8 may not be a good target for antivirals.
PDZD8 does not seem to be a major player in the HIV-1 life cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PDZD8 knockdown experiments that were performed previously should be interpreted with caution.
PDZD8 may be a good marker of retrovirus infectivity but is not a necessary factor for infection.
the PDZD8 protein is not essential for HIV-1 replication.
